hierarchy-bundles.visual_critic_note: Intentional muted palette and polished card/control UI lift it above generic defaults, but the bundle lines are nearly invisible against opaque filled circles — the demo's signature feature is its least legible element.
hierarchy-bundles.encoding_integrity_note: Encoding is structurally honest — scaleSqrt used correctly for sunburst radii and force node size, pack layout handles area internally — but bundle path and hierarchy link data joins lack key functions, risking visual corruption on dataset regeneration, and the force node size scale has a hardcoded domain of [0,200].
flags: Update Storm: mouseenter/mouseleave call full render() without RAF or debounce — at ~200 nodes + 300 bundle paths this triggers expensive DOM joins on every pixel of hover movement
Update Storm: force simulation tick calls render() at ~60fps with no RAF coalescing — full drawBundles()+drawNodes()+drawLabels() on each tick
Mouse-Touch Fight: no touch event handling or event.preventDefault() — drag and hover listeners have no pointer-type guards, causing double-trigger on mobile
hierarchy-bundles.stress_test_note: Hover and force-tick paths skip RAF coalescing (only the bundle slider is throttled), and there is no touch/mouse deduplication, but interrupt() is correctly used before layout transitions and no infinite dispatch loops exist.
hierarchy-bundles.cognitive_load_note: Circle pack view is clean and readable — 3 visible color groups separate well, 300 bundled edges are effectively suppressed at 0.18 opacity until interaction, and controls are organized — but animation quality across 200-node layout transitions and force layout density cannot be assessed from a static screenshot.
